ci-01.cron_text:
# /etc/crontab: system-wide crontab
# Unlike any other crontab you don't have to run the `crontab'
# command to install the new version when you edit this file
# and files in /etc/cron.d. These files also have username fields,
# that none of the other crontabs do.

SHELL=/bin/sh
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/sbin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin

# Example of job definition:
# .---------------- minute (0 - 59)
# |  .------------- hour (0 - 23)
# |  |  .---------- day of month (1 - 31)
# |  |  |  .------- month (1 - 12) OR jan,feb,mar,apr ...
# |  |  |  |  .---- day of week (0 - 6) (Sunday=0 or 7) OR sun,mon,tue,wed,thu,fri,sat
# |  |  |  |  |
# *  *  *  *  * user-name command to be executed
17 *	* * *	root	cd / && run-parts --report /etc/cron.hourly
25 6	* * *	root	test -x /usr/sbin/anacron || { cd / && run-parts --report /etc/cron.daily; }
47 6	* * 7	root	test -x /usr/sbin/anacron || { cd / && run-parts --report /etc/cron.weekly; }
52 6	1 * *	root	test -x /usr/sbin/anacron || { cd / && run-parts --report /etc/cron.monthly; }
#
# DO NOT EDIT OR REMOVE
# This file is a simple placeholder to keep dpkg from removing this directory
30 3 * * 0 root test -e /run/systemd/system || SERVICE_MODE=1 /usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/e2fsprogs/e2scrub_all_cron
10 3 * * * root test -e /run/systemd/system || SERVICE_MODE=1 /sbin/e2scrub_all -A -r
SHELL=/bin/sh
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
# Put the current release on web-01
*/3 * * * *  deploy  /usr/local/bin/larkspur-release >> /var/log/larkspur-release.log 2>&1
# Host maintenance steps
*/4 * * * *  root    /usr/local/sbin/larkspur-maint >> /var/log/larkspur-maint.log 2>&1
# The database archives db-01 sends here go to the offsite bucket
41 * * * *   root    /usr/local/sbin/larkspur-offsite >> /var/log/larkspur-offsite.log 2>&1

SHELL=/bin/sh
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
# Dump the databases and push the archive to ci-01
*/10 * * * *  root  /usr/local/sbin/larkspur-dbdump >> /var/log/larkspur-dbdump.log 2>&1
# Settle the invoices the gateway paid and count what is open
*/15 * * * *  root  /usr/local/sbin/larkspur-invoices >> /var/log/larkspur-invoices.log 2>&1
# Old binary logs
7 3 * * *     root  find /var/log/mysql -name 'mysql-bin.*' -mtime +7 -delete
# Settlement export for the bookkeeper
*/3 * * * *   root  /usr/local/sbin/larkspur-settle >> /var/log/larkspur-settle.log 2>&1
# The day's payout batch to the payment gateway
46 23 * * *   root  /usr/local/sbin/larkspur-settle --batch >> /var/log/larkspur-settle.log 2>&1
# The newest archive's manifest straight to the offsite bucket
*/5 * * * *   root  /usr/local/sbin/larkspur-offsite-copy >> /var/log/larkspur-offsite-copy.log 2>&1
# One archive a night, kept here and on ci-01
12 2 * * *    root  /usr/local/sbin/larkspur-nightly >> /var/log/larkspur-dbdump.log 2>&1

SHELL=/bin/sh
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
# Database dump and copy to the offsite box
17 * * * *   root  /usr/local/sbin/offsite-backup >> /var/log/offsite-backup.log 2>&1
# WordPress scheduled tasks
*/5 * * * *  www-data  cd /var/www/larkspur && php wp-cron.php >/dev/null 2>&1
# Shop numbers for node_exporter (textfile collector)
*/2 * * * *  root  /usr/local/sbin/larkspur-metrics
# Clear expired WordPress transients
*/10 * * * * www-data  cd /var/www/larkspur && /usr/local/bin/wp transient delete --expired --quiet >/dev/null 2>&1
# Shop numbers from the database, for the dashboard
*/2 * * * *  root  /usr/local/sbin/larkspur-orders >> /var/log/larkspur-orders.log 2>&1
# Payout reconciliation against the billing database
*/4 * * * *  root  /usr/local/sbin/larkspur-payouts >> /var/log/larkspur-payouts.log 2>&1
# Numbers for the weekly report
*/3 * * * *  root  /usr/local/sbin/larkspur-report >> /var/log/larkspur-report.log 2>&1
# Rental stock counts for the dashboard
*/30 * * * *  deploy  /opt/larkspur/bin/stock-sync >> /var/log/larkspur-stock.log 2>&1
# /etc/cron.d/php@PHP_VERSION@: crontab fragment for PHP
#  This purges session files in session.save_path older than X,
#  where X is defined in seconds as the largest value of
#  session.gc_maxlifetime from all your SAPI php.ini files
#  or 24 minutes if not defined.  The script triggers only
#  when session.save_handler=files.
#
#  WARNING: The scripts tries hard to honour all relevant
#  session PHP options, but if you do something unusual
#  you have to disable this script and take care of your
#  sessions yourself.

# Look for and purge old sessions every 30 minutes
09,39 *     * * *     root   [ -x /usr/lib/php/sessionclean ] && if [ ! -d /run/systemd/system ]; then /usr/lib/php/sessionclean; fi
